static_traits.name: Li Xin
static_traits.family_status: Has two children; both parents from the family of origin are Teachers
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no prior similar psychological problems or psychotherapy history (self-reported)
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to self-Reflect; negative-leaning tone, with self-blame and catastrophizing tendencies; report mentions avoiding related topics and situations; cooperativeness fair but Reserved and skeptical about change

basic_info.main_problem: Feeling like a 'bad parent' for not yet taking the children hunting; this guilt and Continuing self-doubt have lasted months, recurring when Thinking about spending quality time with children, and affecting mood and parent-child interaction.
basic_info.core_demands: Seeking counseling because parenting guilt and Self-doubt are affecting mood and interaction with children; hoping to ease these emotions and improve time with the children.
growth_experiences: Both parents in the family of origin are Teachers; no significant physical or mental illness and no prior psychotherapy history (self-reported).

core_beliefs: I am an unqualified / not-good-enough parent
My worth depends on whether I meet others'/society's expectations of a 'good parent'

special_situations.event: When seeing other parents frequently carrying out various activities with their children, compares
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not done many activities with the children like other parents, it means I am a failure, an incompetent parent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding social situations and topics that remind me of 'not doing enough', self-blaming and trying to prove myself by scheduling more activities (but often avoiding due to stress)
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them; I am a bad parent

special_situations.event: Triggering guilt and Self-doubt when Thinking about spending quality time with children
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: A 'good parent' should share every part of life with the children; if I have not shared everything, it equals failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Demands of herself with 'should / must' rules, includes hunting in the parent-child activity plan, but avoids it because of pressure and worry.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I do not take them hunting, so I am a bad parent

special_situations.event: When the child makes a request to go out, accumulated guilt leads to losing temper at the child
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot stay patient and perform perfectly at all times, it proves I am a bad parent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing the risk of being discovered 'incompetent' by keeping distance and detachment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I hurt him again; everything It is all my fault

special_situations.event: Considering inviting the children to hunt but worrying they will not like it
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the children do not like my hobby, it means I am even more of a failure, and our relationship will get worse
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids trying or talking about hunting to evade possible disappointment and shame
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They probably will not like it; this will only make things worse

core_conflict.wish: Longs to build a deeper connection with my children and to be seen as a competent, accepted parent
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being judged a 'bad parent' by the children or others, Being rejected and disappointed, thus losing self-worth
defense_goal: Reducing shame and guilt by avoiding triggering topics and situations
Keeping some emotional distance to avoid being judged
Uses self-blame to gain a superficial sense of control over runaway emotions

object_relations.object_representation: Children who may be disappointed in or reject oneself

object_relations.self_representation: An inferior parent who needs to meet standards

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites exploration of the core belief about 'bad parents' and feelings of guilt
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Subconsciously understanding exploration as judgment or 'scrutiny', fearing being labeled an unqualified parent
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responds by analyzing and discussing 'social expectations/theory', tone restrained and somewhat objective, reducing narration of emotional expression and body sensations.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When recalling specific scenes of yelling at the children or poor parent-child interactions
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Over-attributing negative outcomes to self, thinking 'everything It is all my fault', fearing being negated by others
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing Self-blame and guilt, using expressions like 'it is all my fault', in a low tone, avoiding exploring needs behind emotions and situational context.

manifestations: Requiring oneself with 'should/must' to share every part of life with the children, equating choices and responsibility with moral obligation
Internalizing social expectations as evaluation standards, worrying that a choice not accepted by the children means failure
outcomes: Avoiding discussing hunting topics with the children
Interactions with the child show irritability and distance, with a decreased sense of connection

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Repeatedly using self-Demands like 'should/must' (like 'I should share every part of my life with the children')
Uses society's expectations of a 'good parent' as the sole yardstick for self-evaluation

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Strong self-blame and Self-doubt, avoiding expressing true needs for fear of being seen as a 'bad parent'
Being reserved and pessimistic when discussing change, cautious and not daring to try

exception_events.target_problem: When Thinking about spending quality time with children, Li Xin is usually trapped by the guilt of 'I do not take them hunting = I am a bad parent', thus avoiding or becoming irritable and distant in interactions.
exception_events.unique_outcome: During family interactions playing board games or cooking with the children, Li Xin was not dominated by 'bad parent' thoughts, but could focus on the present, experiencing connection and engagement.
exception_events.reason: Clues: when activities do not involve the trigger theme of 'hunting', external evaluation frameworks and 'should' rules are not activated; different approach: focusing on shared fun and present interaction, rather than self-evaluation.

positive_force: Able to maintain varied daily interactions with the child (such as board games, cooking)
Having self-awareness and Reflection ability, able to identify guilt and negative thought patterns
Actively seeks help, willing to explore and try small-step changes in counseling
negative_force: Internalizing social expectations as self-evaluation standards (Introjection)
Catastrophizing and personalization thinking, accompanied by 'should' rules
Avoiding trigger situations to briefly ease guilt, long-term Reinforcing the problem
Excessive comparison with others leads to inferiority and shame

target_behavior.behavior: Irritability and distance triggered by parenting guilt
antecedent: Thinking about spending quality time with children
Sees scenes of other parents doing activities with children
The child requests outings or joint activities
target_behavior.core_reason: Directly equating 'not yet taking children hunting' with 'incompetent parent', driven by Introjected social expectations and 'should' beliefs, accompanied by catastrophizing and personalization cognitions
target_behavior.function: Avoids being judged and feelings of shame, briefly reducing guilt
target_behavior.consequence: Declining parent-child interaction quality, increased irritability and distance, further Reinforcing self-blame and negative cycles

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids hunting-related topics and parent-child activity plans
antecedent: Mentioning or thinking about hunting and children's participation
Self-comparison and worry when planning time with the children
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying children will not like it or others will judge, believing outcomes will be worse, thus avoiding to prevent disappointment and shame
target_behavior.function: Briefly easing Anxiety and guilt (negative Reinforcement)
target_behavior.consequence: Reduces opportunities for positive parent-child experiences, maintaining and reinforcing the belief 'I am a bad parent'
